name: Abū ʿAlī ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī al-Ishbīlī al-Shalawbīn
summary: The teacher of Seville for some sixty years, master of Ibn ʿUṣfūr and of the last great generation of Andalusian grammarians.
bio: Al-Shalawbīn was born in Seville in 562/1166; his name is a Romance word of al-Andalus meaning 'the fair'. He taught grammar in Seville for about sixty years, and most of the Andalusian grammarians of the next generation, Ibn ʿUṣfūr above all, sat with him.
His short al-Tawṭiʾa is a handbook, and he wrote two commentaries on al-Jazūlī's difficult al-Muqaddima. He left Seville shortly before it fell to Castile and died in 645/1247.
